title: Gain-boosted cascode OTA
description: A cascode OTA whose cascode devices are regulated by auxiliary 'booster' amplifiers (gain-boosting / regulated cascode). A booster senses the cascoded device's drain and drives the cascode gate to hold its source fixed, so the local feedback multiplies the cascode's own intrinsic gain by the booster gain: each side's output resistance becomes about $A_{v0,boost} * A_{v0,casc} * r_o$. That lifts the single-stage gain by the booster gain — often 20-40 dB — without adding a stack device or a second signal-path pole. The price is the booster's own bandwidth: it forms a pole-zero doublet that slows settling, so the closed-loop settling is estimate-grade and the sim owns sign-off. The stack is parameterized by its NODES: the tail node is solved so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$, and the internal nodes $V_a$ (input drain) and $V_b$ (mirror drain) are choice params — every device $V_{DS}$ is a subtraction between adjacent nodes, every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias, and the drops sum to the rail by construction. The tail is drawn: a diode-connected bias reference carries the programmed $I_{tail}$, the tail device sits on that reference's gate at that reference's width with the tail node as its drain, and the pair carries half of what the tail delivers there — so the low end of the common-mode range is where the tail device runs out of drain-source voltage, and a check says so. Here one booster child models the regulation gain and is applied to both the NMOS and PMOS output cascodes. The output is single-ended, through a current-mirror load whose two devices share a gate on the diode side's output node — where the diode side's two cascodes meet — so that node sits one mirror $V_{GS}$ below the supply while the output sits at $V_{out,dc}$, held there by the feedback the application closes around the amplifier. The diode side's cascodes sit on the same node levels as the output side's, their sources held at $V_a$ and $V_b$ like their partners' (the diode side's output node is low-impedance, so those cascodes are biased there rather than boosted for gain), and they are drawn as blocks of their own because their drains sit at that node rather than at the output. Everything under and over them is the same on both sides: the two pair transistors share a drain level, a source and a current, and so do the two mirror devices, so each pair is one sizing placed twice, the tail current splits evenly, and there is no systematic offset to report.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget; with each device's noise read from the tables, the row lands near 26.9 nV/rtHz on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table, the pair receiving less than the programmed tail current — just over this budget. No simulated floor exists for this topology

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low end — checked exactly by the cm-lo range end at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.87-1.24 V on sky130 tt with the PMOS devices on the pfet table, at the shipped choices, the low end set by the tail device leaving saturation and the high end by the pair). The range end checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis. The slider stops where the stack does: with V_a holding the pair's drain low, the tail node cannot climb past its range and the topology genuinely cannot take a higher CM — the telescopic's known input-range ceiling

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS nodes climb to it and the PMOS nodes descend to it. The two gain-boosted cascodes meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source and the tail device's drain. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. An end of the range where the relation does not evaluate — the top end, where it leaves the pair too little room below V_a to size — is stepped inward silently, and the searched range is reported only if the search then fails; the input device declares that it must stay saturated, so its own saturation check owns that

params.name: V_a
params.note: the NMOS-side internal node: input drain and NMOS-cascode source. The input vds is V_a - V_tail and the cascode's is V_out_dc - V_a, by construction. The NMOS-side booster holds this node: it is an amplifier with its own reference voltage, applied from outside this sheet, and this value is that reference

params.name: V_b
params.note: the PMOS-side internal node: mirror drain and PMOS-cascode source, on both sides. The mirror vds is VDD - V_b and the output-side cascode's is V_b - V_out_dc, by construction; the diode-side cascode's is what is left above the mirror's gate, one mirror V_GS below the supply, which has to cover its saturation voltage — the default sits high for that. The PMOS-side booster holds this node: it is an amplifier with its own reference voltage, applied from outside this sheet, and this value is that reference

params.name: avt
params.note: Pelgrom A_VT

params.name: abeta
params.note: Pelgrom A_beta

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one tail current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node normally sits below the reference's diode drop); slew rate, bandwidth and supply current are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: I_boost
params.note: booster tail current; sets the booster bandwidth (settling doublet) — spend enough to keep it faster than the main loop

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: sets the un-boosted cascode gain av0_casc

params.name: gm_id_mir
params.note: load-mirror inversion: lower gm/ID gives higher mirror ro, but the mirror's gate is the diode side's output node, one mirror V_GS below the supply, and the diode side's NMOS cascode needs its saturation voltage between that node and V_a — at 8 a PMOS table's V_GS leaves it in triode, so the default sits at 13

params.name: gm_id_bo
params.note: booster-device inversion: sets the booster gain that multiplies each cascode's ro

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: higher V* costs CM-low headroom. Set as weak as the pair's, because this stack's common mode sits low: at gm/ID 10 the tail device needs more drain-source voltage than the low end of the claimed range leaves it on sky130 tt

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference and of the tail device, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirror's drain-voltage error

params.name: vds_bo
params.note: booster output-device vds. Stated by the designer: the one booster child stands for both regulating amplifiers, NMOS side and PMOS side, and of their circuits only one stand-in gain device is on this sheet

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_{tail}$ flows into — the one device in the main branch whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device needs to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with the tail node as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Input-pair devices
doc.description: The two pair transistors, one sizing placed twice: each carries half of what the tail delivers, and the boosters hold both drains at V_a, so the two sit at one operating point. The output side's ro is boosted by its NMOS cascode and that cascode's booster.

doc.title: NMOS output cascode
doc.description: Regulated cascode over the input device; its intrinsic gain av0, times the booster gain, sets the NMOS-side Rout.

doc.title: PMOS output cascode
doc.description: Regulated cascode over the load mirror; its intrinsic gain av0, times the booster gain, sets the PMOS-side Rout.

doc.title: Load mirror devices
doc.description: The two sides of the PMOS load mirror, one sizing placed twice: each carries the current of the pair transistor in its branch, both drains are held at V_b, and both gates sit on the diode side's output node, one $V_{GS}$ below the supply. The output side's ro, cascoded and boosted, sets the PMOS-side output resistance.

doc.title: NMOS cascode, diode side
doc.description: The diode side's NMOS cascode: the output-side cascode's width, carrying the diode-side pair transistor's current, its source held at V_a like its partner's. Its drain is the diode side's output node — the mirror's gate, one mirror $V_{GS}$ below the supply — rather than the output, so its gate-source voltage is read off the table at that drain voltage, and its saturation is checked there.

params.name: W_c
params.note: the output-side cascode's width

doc.title: PMOS cascode, diode side
doc.description: The diode side's PMOS cascode: the output-side cascode's width, carrying the diode side's current, its source held at V_b like its partner's. Its drain is the diode side's output node, which is the mirror's gate, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between V_b and one mirror $V_{GS}$ below the supply, and its saturation is checked there. Its body bias is VDD - V_b (the PMOS tables' vsb axis carries that magnitude).

params.name: W_c
params.note: the output-side cascode's width

doc.title: Gain-boost amplifier
doc.description: The regulating auxiliary amp, modelled as a single gain stage; its DC gain av0 multiplies each cascode's intrinsic gain, and its own ft (gm/2*pi*cgg) sets the settling doublet.

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: Rout_n
equations.note: NMOS side: input ro boosted by the cascode gain and again by the booster gain

equations.name: Rout_p
equations.note: PMOS side: mirror ro boosted by the cascode gain and again by the booster gain

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the two regulated-cascode sides in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered into the load — the current the tail device delivers, not the number the reference is programmed to

equations.name: f_boost
equations.note: estimate: the booster's own ft, a proxy for its bandwidth; the doublet near this frequency governs settling

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: input pair plus the load mirror's own density referred by gm_mir/gm_in; the boosters sit outside the main signal path and add little

equations.name: vos
equations.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, mir__W, L_mir, gm_id_mir)*mir__gm/in__gm)^2)
equations.note: input-pair offset plus the load-mirror offset referred by the gm ratio

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact here, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the main branch at the current the tail device delivers plus one booster per cascode polarity, as these rows model them. The reference branch that programs the tail is shared bias infrastructure, typically one reference feeding several stages, and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

checks.note: reads each device's thermal noise from the table where the table carries it, and the gamma = 1 estimate where it does not; it stays advisory because a sheet cannot know which table it will be evaluated on, and the simulator owns noise sign-off
estimate: the booster must be faster than the main loop or its doublet slows settling; sim owns the real settling
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges check that the design covers the range ENDS, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve over its full range, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every hard rule must hold there

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way. The edges check the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
